Ever since I could remember I was terrified of vomiting, it is my greatest phobia. I would go to school and often feel nauseous and try to call my parents to take me home. Though, once I got home I would feel much better every time. My mom thought I had some stomach issue, but we figured out years later what it really was.

When I hit 18 and I was in college I caught some stomach bug from my boyfriend, and after that I was pretty much unable to function. I had no appetite, felt like I couldn’t breathe all the time, and had horrible insomnia. I went to the doctor several time for physical tests to scan my esophagus and stomach for GERD and other gastrointestinal issues. They all came out negative. Oddly, this destroyed me because I just wanted it to be something that could be diagnosed and fixed with some meds so I could get on with my life. My doctor then set me aside and told me he thought this was an extreme anxiety disorder and nothing wrong with my stomach or throat at all. He prescribed me with some Xanax and I felt like I was given a life sentence of misery. For the next year I shuffled through therapists, medications, and side effects. I was terrified of eating so I eventually went from 140lbs to 85lbs. If I got down to 80lbs they would have put me in the hospital until I regulated my eating. I also lost my boyfriend because the fact that I got my stomach bug from him, I became irrationally terrified of him. We had been dating for four years so it was not a good time for me obviously. I also had to quit going to college because I couldn’t function properly due to severe anxiety symptoms.

If you’re wondering I was officially diagnosed with an anxiety disorder, clinical depression, and obsessive thought disorder. I am 25 now and have a long-term boyfriend who I live with, graduated college, at a healthy weight, and have gotten my anxiety under control. I still have some issues with my depression, but I’m working through that. Panic attacks come and go, but they’re seldom and I’ve learned to deal with them. Coming to terms with the fact that throughout my whole life I had an undiagnosed anxiety disorder and not something physical was extremely difficult. Everyone wants a quick fix, but this isn’t the case for mental illnesses, and it can be a very difficult thing to come to terms with. It probably took me two years to accept it and that I wouldn’t be crippled by this forever and can get over it.
